messages.content: You design amateur rockets that fly on certified commercial motors. Work through the design, check it with the tools, and give the final design as JSON inside <design> tags. Only report results the tools returned.
Three-stage rocket, nothing bigger than a C motor in any stage. Looking for roughly 650 m. It needs to come down at 6 m/s or less. What would you build?

messages.reasoning_content:
1. Understand: three stages, and no motor in any stage may be bigger than a C. Apogee is roughly 650 m, so the band is 650 * 0.95 = 618 m to 650 * 1.05 = 682 m. Every stage has to land at 6 m/s or less, so each one needs its own recovery. Rail and wind are not stated. I assume a 1.5 m rail, 2 m/s wind, vertical, sea level.
2. Feasibility: three C motors are about 30 N*s if they are the small black-powder ones, and a three-stage stack is heavy for a 6 N motor. Drag-free speed for 650 m is sqrt(2 * 9.81 * 650) = 113 m/s, so the motors have to be the biggest C class and the airframe has to be light. I need the thrust and diameter of a few C motors before I pick one for each stage.

2. Feasibility: Estes C6 is only 8.8 N*s at 4.8 N, and the C11 is the same 8.8 N*s in a heavier 24 mm case. AeroTech C18W is 9.8 N*s at 19.3 N, 18 mm, 0.081 m long, 0.021 kg, and it has no 0 s delay. Three of them are 3 * 9.8 = 29 N*s. That is still a small budget for 650 m, so the airframe stays 22 mm and short, and every motor is plugged so separation is at burnout rather than a delay charge. The C18W thrust clears a 1.5 m rail that a C6 stack would not.
3. Size: guessed stack mass 0.11 kg. Booster thrust-to-weight is 19.3 / (0.11 * 9.81) = 18. Each spent stage is about 0.04 kg. A 5 m/s landing, under the 6 m/s limit, needs 2 * 0.04 * 9.81 / (1.225 * 0.8 * 5^2) = 0.032 m^2, diameter sqrt(4 * 0.032 / 3.1416) = 0.20 m. I'll fit a 0.22 m chute on every stage.
4. Draft: sustainer 0.25 m with the nose and small fins, a 0.14 m middle stage, and a 0.16 m booster with larger fins so the stack margin stays positive. All three motors are C18W, upper stages light at burnout, lower stages separate at burnout. Defaults: 1.5 m rail, 2 m/s wind.

messages.reasoning_content:
4. Check: the simulator gives apogee 649.1 m. The target is 650 m, and 650 - 649.1 = 0.9 m, inside the 5% band of 0.05 * 650 = 32 m. Landings are 4.1, 3.6 and 3.8 m/s, all under 6. Rail exit is 26.0 m/s, thrust-to-weight is 19.5, rail margin is 2.6 cal, and the burn minimum is 1.17 cal. Every stage opened its chute. All three motors are C18W. The open-forward-airframe note is the separated booster tube. Every check passes.
5. Fix: no fix was needed.
6. Uncertainty: 0.9 m under 650 m is a tight match, and a heavier build than the 0.101 kg liftoff mass will fall out of the 5% band. Margin dips to 1.17 cal while the upper motors burn, still above 1.0, but a gust could eat that. Chute Cd is a model 0.8. Wind was assumed at 2 m/s. Mach 0.87 is high for cardboard, and the drag model is less sure there.
